tasks.notes:
# Task #18: `ralph task next-id [--count <n>]` CLI command

## What was done
Added a `next-id` subcommand to the `task` group plus an exported, testable
handler, following the existing `taskAdd`/`taskShow` pattern.

### `src/commands/task.ts`
- New import: `reserveTaskIds` from `../task-counter`.
- New exported handler `taskNextId(opts: TaskNextIdOpts): number`:
  - `TaskNextIdOpts = { count?: number; dataDir: string; stdout?: Writer; stderr?: Writer }`
  - `count` defaults to 1.
  - Validates `Number.isInteger(count) && count >= 1`; on failure writes
    `ralph task next-id: --count must be a positive integer, got <count>\n`
    to stderr and returns exit code 1 — **before** touching state.json
    (so no reservation/state write happens on invalid input).
  - Calls `reserveTaskIds(dataDir, count)` and prints the ids one per line
    (`ids.join('\n') + '\n'`) to stdout, returns 0.
  - Wraps `reserveTaskIds` in try/catch and surfaces errors on stderr → exit 1.
- CLI wiring in `registerTaskCommands`: `task.command('next-id')` with
  `--option('--count <n>', ..., (v) => parseInt(v,10), 1)` (default 1).
  Live command uses the existing `dataDir()` closure (`process.env.RALPH_DATA_DIR`).
  Invalid CLI input like `--count abc` → `parseInt` yields `NaN` → handler
  rejects with exit 1.

### `src/index.ts`
No change needed — `registerTaskCommands(program)` was already wired
(import line 14, call line 182). Confirmed via grep.

## TDD
Added tests to `test/commands/task.test.ts` FIRST, watched them fail with
`Export named 'taskNextId' not found`, then implemented.
New `describe('task next-id')` block (defaultTasks has ids 1,2 so seed → 3):
- (10a) default → prints `3\n`, exit 0.
- (10b) `--count 3` → prints `3\n4\n5\n`; a follow-up call continues at `6\n`
  (proves the counter advanced / persisted across calls in the same dataDir).
- (10c) parametrized over `[0, -2, NaN, 1.5]` → exit 1, stderr matches
  `/ralph task next-id/`, and asserts **no** `state.json` was written on rejection.

## Verification
- `bun test test/commands/task.test.ts` → 28 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test` (full suite) → 707 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run build` → succeeds.

## Heads-up for next agents
- `state.json` is the task-id counter file (`{ "nextTaskId": N }`), created
  lazily on first `reserveTaskIds`. It is **untracked** and not in `.gitignore`.
  If a future task (e.g. init, task 20) wants it ignored or seeded explicitly,
  that's a separate concern.
- Live CLI smoke-testing of `next-id` in this sandbox is awkward: the shell has
  `RALPH_DATA_DIR` exported to the repo's `.ralph`, and inline `VAR=val cmd` /
  `env` overrides did not reach the spawned binary — so smoke runs mutate the
  repo's real counter. The unit tests use isolated tmpdirs and are the reliable
  check. (Any stray `state.json` from such smoke runs should be deleted; I removed
  the one my test created.)

tasks.title: Auto-assign id in ralph task add
tasks.description: Make ralph task add (taskAdd in src/commands/task.ts:218) own id assignment. Inside taskAdd (which has dataDir), call reserveTaskIds(dataDir, 1), inject that id into the parsed payload (overwriting any supplied id — always ignore agent-supplied ids), THEN validate. Because validation runs after injection, the schema's required id is always present, so no schema relaxation is needed. Print the assigned id to stdout (e.g. 'assigned id: <n>') so the agent learns it. Reserve the id only once and reuse it if the mutate retries. Also update the executor prompt in src/commands/run.ts (the DISCOVER AND DOCUMENT block, ~lines 131-133): change it so agents do NOT supply an id — drop id from the 'New tasks need at minimum' list and note the CLI assigns and prints the id. TDD: add tests to test/commands/task.test.ts covering a payload with no id getting a reserved id assigned and appended; a payload WITH an id having it overwritten by the reserved one; and the assigned id being printed to stdout. Write tests first, watch them fail, then implement.

Write tests first, watch them fail, then implement.
